manifests.describe: Check workflow daemon health status.
manifests.longDescription: Performs a health check on the workflow daemon by making an HTTP request to /health endpoint. Use this to verify the daemon is running and responding.

display.name: Workflow CLI
display.description: CLI commands for interacting with KB Labs Workflow Daemon

groupMeta.describe: Workflow run management (list, view, watch, rerun)

commands.describe: Check workflow daemon health status.
commands.longDescription: Performs a health check on the workflow daemon by making an HTTP request to /health endpoint. Use this to verify the daemon is running and responding.

commands.describe: Get workflow daemon metrics.
commands.longDescription: Fetches comprehensive metrics from the workflow daemon including total runs, queued jobs, running jobs, completed jobs, and failure counts.

commands.describe: Validate workflow files against the schema.
commands.longDescription: Statically validates workflow files under .kb/workflows (or a given --path) against WorkflowSpecSchema, reporting per-file issues with their JSON-path. Runs locally without the daemon. Exits non-zero if any file is invalid (or, with --strict, has warnings).

commands.describe: (Deprecated) Get job status. Use: kb workflow runs status <runId>
commands.longDescription: Retrieves detailed status information for a specific job by ID, including current state, start time, and completion time if finished. DEPRECATED: use "kb workflow runs status <runId>" for run-level status.

flags.name: job-id
flags.description: Job ID to get status for

commands.describe: (Deprecated) Get job/run logs. Use: kb workflow runs logs <runId>
commands.longDescription: Fetches execution logs for a specific job or run by ID. DEPRECATED: use "kb workflow runs logs <runId>" for run-level logs.

flags.name: job-id
flags.description: Job ID to get logs for (required)

commands.describe: (Deprecated) List active executions. Use: kb workflow runs list
commands.longDescription: Lists all currently active workflow executions or cron jobs. Can be filtered by status (running, queued, completed, failed, cancelled) or type (runs, cron). DEPRECATED: use "kb workflow runs list" for run listing.

commands.describe: Submit a raw job for execution.
commands.longDescription: Submits a job to the workflow daemon for execution. Requires a handler (plugin command) and optionally accepts input parameters as JSON. Can wait for job completion with --wait flag.

commands.describe: List workflow runs.
commands.longDescription: Lists workflow runs with status, trigger, and duration. Filter by status (failed, running, success) or workflow ID. Use --json for machine-readable output.

flags.name: status
flags.description: Filter by status: failed, running, success, queued, cancelled

flags.name: limit
flags.description: Maximum number of runs to show (default: 20)

flags.name: workflow
flags.description: Filter by workflow ID or name

commands.describe: View run details for incident investigation.
commands.longDescription: Shows full run details: jobs, steps, resolvedInputs, gate decisions, errors. Without a run ID shows the latest run (like gh run view). Use --log-failed to see only the logs from failed steps (fastest path to root cause). Use --json=status,jobs for selective JSON output.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to inspect (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: json
flags.description: Output specific fields as JSON. Use --json (no value) or --json=all for full output, or --json=field1,field2 for selective fields.

flags.name: log-failed
flags.description: Show logs only from failed steps (most useful for investigation)

flags.name: step
flags.description: Filter logs to a specific step name

commands.describe: Stream workflow run events in real-time.
commands.longDescription: Connects to the run event stream via SSE and prints events as they happen. Without a run ID watches the latest run (like gh run watch). Automatically exits when the run finishes.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to watch (alias for positional argument)

commands.describe: Rerun a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Reruns a workflow by re-submitting it with the same inputs. Use --failed-only to requeue only jobs that failed or were interrupted.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to rerun (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: failed-only
flags.description: Rerun only jobs that failed or were interrupted

commands.describe: Restart a run from a specific step.
commands.longDescription: Restores the run from a snapshot and re-executes from the given step. All preceding steps inherit their stored outputs without being re-run. Omitting --from-step restarts from step 1 using the snapshot env.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to restart (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: from-step
flags.description: Step ID to restart from; all preceding steps inherit their stored outputs

commands.describe: Cancel a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Cancels an active workflow run. If the run is not found or already finished, prints a clear error.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to cancel (alias for positional argument)

commands.describe: Fetch logs for a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Fetches execution logs for a run. Use --log-failed to show only failed-step logs. Use --step to filter to a specific step. Accepts a positional run ID or --run-id flag.

flags.name: step
flags.description: Filter logs to a specific step name

flags.name: log-failed
flags.description: Show only logs from failed steps

commands.describe: Show status summary for a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Displays the status of a run including jobs and steps. Accepts a positional run ID or --run-id flag.

commands.describe: Approve or reject a pending approval step in a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Resolves a human-gate (approval) step that is waiting for a decision. If the run has exactly one pending approval, it is resolved automatically. If there are multiple, specify --job-id and --step-id to target the right one. Use --action=reject to reject instead of approve (default: approve). Use --comment to attach a note to the decision.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to approve/reject (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: job-id
flags.description: Job ID containing the approval step

flags.name: step-id
flags.description: Step ID to approve or reject

flags.name: comment
flags.description: Optional comment to attach to the approval decision

commands.describe: Run workflow by ID.
commands.longDescription: Runs a workflow definition by workflow ID via /api/v1/workflows/:id/run endpoint. Supports request-level target and isolation overrides.

flags.name: input
flags.description: JSON string of workflow input payload

flags.name: isolation
flags.description: Isolation profile: strict, balanced, or relaxed

flags.name: trigger-type
flags.description: Trigger type: manual, api, or cron

flags.name: status
flags.description: Filter by status: failed, running, success, queued, cancelled

flags.name: limit
flags.description: Maximum number of runs to show (default: 20)

flags.name: workflow
flags.description: Filter by workflow ID or name

commands.describe: View run details for incident investigation.
commands.longDescription: Shows full run details: jobs, steps, resolvedInputs, gate decisions, errors. Without a run ID shows the latest run (like gh run view). Use --log-failed to see only the logs from failed steps (fastest path to root cause). Use --json=status,jobs for selective JSON output.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to inspect (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: json
flags.description: Output specific fields as JSON. Use --json (no value) or --json=all for full output, or --json=field1,field2 for selective fields.

flags.name: log-failed
flags.description: Show logs only from failed steps (most useful for investigation)

flags.name: step
flags.description: Filter logs to a specific step name

commands.describe: Stream workflow run events in real-time.
commands.longDescription: Connects to the run event stream via SSE and prints events as they happen. Without a run ID watches the latest run (like gh run watch). Automatically exits when the run finishes.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to watch (alias for positional argument)

commands.describe: Rerun a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Reruns a workflow by re-submitting it with the same inputs. Use --failed-only to requeue only jobs that failed or were interrupted.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to rerun (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: failed-only
flags.description: Rerun only jobs that failed or were interrupted

commands.describe: Restart a run from a specific step.
commands.longDescription: Restores the run from a snapshot and re-executes from the given step. All preceding steps inherit their stored outputs without being re-run. Omitting --from-step restarts from step 1 using the snapshot env.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to restart (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: from-step
flags.description: Step ID to restart from; all preceding steps inherit their stored outputs

commands.describe: Cancel a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Cancels an active workflow run. If the run is not found or already finished, prints a clear error.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to cancel (alias for positional argument)

commands.describe: Fetch logs for a workflow run.

flags.name: step
flags.description: Filter logs to a specific step name

flags.description: Show only logs from failed steps

commands.describe: Show status summary for a workflow run.

flags.name: job-id
flags.description: Job ID containing the approval step

flags.name: step-id
flags.description: Step ID to approve or reject

flags.name: comment
flags.description: Optional comment to attach to the approval decision

commands.longDescription: Shows full run details: jobs, steps, resolvedInputs, gate decisions, errors. Without a run ID shows the latest run (like gh run view). Use --log-failed to see only the logs from failed steps (fastest path to root cause). Use --json=status,jobs for selective JSON output.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to inspect (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: json
flags.description: Output specific fields as JSON. Use --json (no value) or --json=all for full output, or --json=field1,field2 for selective fields.

flags.name: log-failed
flags.description: Show logs only from failed steps (most useful for investigation)

flags.name: step
flags.description: Filter logs to a specific step name

commands.describe: Stream workflow run events in real-time.
commands.longDescription: Connects to the run event stream via SSE and prints events as they happen. Without a run ID watches the latest run (like gh run watch). Automatically exits when the run finishes.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to watch (alias for positional argument)

commands.describe: Rerun a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Reruns a workflow by re-submitting it with the same inputs. Use --failed-only to requeue only jobs that failed or were interrupted.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to rerun (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: failed-only
flags.description: Rerun only jobs that failed or were interrupted

commands.describe: Restart a run from a specific step.
commands.longDescription: Restores the run from a snapshot and re-executes from the given step. All preceding steps inherit their stored outputs without being re-run. Omitting --from-step restarts from step 1 using the snapshot env.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to restart (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: from-step
flags.description: Step ID to restart from; all preceding steps inherit their stored outputs

commands.describe: Cancel a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Cancels an active workflow run. If the run is not found or already finished, prints a clear error.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to cancel (alias for positional argument)

commands.describe: Fetch logs for a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Fetches execution logs for a run. Use --log-failed to show only failed-step logs. Use --step to filter to a specific step. Accepts a positional run ID or --run-id flag.

flags.name: step
flags.description: Filter logs to a specific step name

flags.name: log-failed
flags.description: Show only logs from failed steps

commands.describe: Show status summary for a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Displays the status of a run including jobs and steps. Accepts a positional run ID or --run-id flag.

commands.describe: Approve or reject a pending approval step in a workflow run.
commands.longDescription: Resolves a human-gate (approval) step that is waiting for a decision. If the run has exactly one pending approval, it is resolved automatically. If there are multiple, specify --job-id and --step-id to target the right one. Use --action=reject to reject instead of approve (default: approve). Use --comment to attach a note to the decision.

flags.name: run-id
flags.description: Run ID to approve/reject (alias for positional argument)

flags.name: job-id
flags.description: Job ID containing the approval step

flags.name: step-id
flags.description: Step ID to approve or reject

flags.name: comment
flags.description: Optional comment to attach to the approval decision

commands.describe: Run workflow by ID.
commands.longDescription: Runs a workflow definition by workflow ID via /api/v1/workflows/:id/run endpoint. Supports request-level target and isolation overrides.

flags.name: input
flags.description: JSON string of workflow input payload

flags.name: isolation
flags.description: Isolation profile: strict, balanced, or relaxed

flags.name: trigger-type
flags.description: Trigger type: manual, api, or cron

commands.describe: Pack the currently-committed package versions for a flow into real npm tarballs, once, for `release deliver` to ship
commands.longDescription: Produces the actual npm tarball artifacts for a flow's already-committed package.json versions — no re-bump, no rebuild. Writes a manifest.json (name/version/tarball/sha256) alongside the tarballs. Intended to run once in CI right after checking out a release tag; every `release deliver` target then ships these exact bytes instead of re-packing independently. Not the same command as `release pack` (that one verifies proposed packages before a release is decided; this one packs an already-decided one).

flags.name: release-tag
flags.description: Git tag to resolve {flow, channel} from (via release.flows[*].tagPattern) — alternative to --flow

flags.name: flow
flags.description: Named flow — selects packages the same way `release run --flow` does (e.g. excludes sdk from platform)

commands.describe: Install a packed tarball into a throwaway consumer and confirm it imports cleanly
commands.longDescription: Installs --tarball into a fresh, outside-the-workspace consumer project and confirms --name can be imported afterward. Shared by check-pack-install.sh (local release gate) and `release stage` (CI publish path) so both use identical verification — catches an already-published PEER dependency that is itself broken, which static manifest checks cannot see. Surfaces the real failure reason via @npmcli/arborist directly; plain `npm install` swallows this exact failure class as an unhandled rejection with no usable error.

flags.name: tarball
flags.description: Path to the packed tarball to install

flags.name: name
flags.description: Package name to import after install

commands.describe: Promote already-released package versions to npm (no re-bump, no rebuild)
commands.longDescription: Publishes the CURRENT on-disk package.json versions to npm — no version bump, no rebuild. Intended to run after `release run --channel stable` (typically targeting Verdaccio via config.registry): once that run is verified, `release promote` pushes the exact same, already-committed versions to npm under the stable dist-tag.

flags.name: flow
flags.description: Named flow — selects packages the same way `release run --flow` does (e.g. excludes sdk from platform)

flags.name: tag
flags.description: npm dist-tag override (default: config.publish.stableTag, falls back to "latest")

flags.name: registry
flags.description: Registry override (default: config.publish.npmRegistry, falls back to real npm)

flags.name: otp
flags.description: One-time password (optional, will prompt if needed)

commands.describe: Ship the tarballs `release stage` already packed to a target — no packing, no rebuild
commands.longDescription: CI-side half of the "plugin prepares, CI delivers" release flow: reads manifest.json written by `release stage` and ships those exact tarballs to --target (only "npm" is implemented this pass). Resolves {flow, channel} from --release-tag via release.flows[*].tagPattern so CI never needs to guess the flow itself — just pass the tag. Verifies the delivery against the real registry afterwards (with retry, since real npm has propagation lag); never attempts npm unpublish on a verification failure — that is a human decision.

flags.description: Git tag to resolve {flow, channel} from (via release.flows[*].tagPattern) — alternative to --flow

flags.name: target
flags.description: Delivery target (default: npm — the only target implemented this pass)

flags.description: npm dist-tag override (default: config.publish.stableTag, falls back to "latest")

flags.name: registry
flags.description: Registry override (default: config.publish.npmRegistry, falls back to real npm)

flags.description: One-time password (optional, will prompt if needed)

commands.describe: Pack the currently-committed package versions for a flow into real npm tarballs, once, for `release deliver` to ship
commands.longDescription: Produces the actual npm tarball artifacts for a flow's already-committed package.json versions — no re-bump, no rebuild. Writes a manifest.json (name/version/tarball/sha256) alongside the tarballs. Intended to run once in CI right after checking out a release tag; every `release deliver` target then ships these exact bytes instead of re-packing independently. Not the same command as `release pack` (that one verifies proposed packages before a release is decided; this one packs an already-decided one).

commands.describe: Install a packed tarball into a throwaway consumer and confirm it imports cleanly
commands.longDescription: Installs --tarball into a fresh, outside-the-workspace consumer project and confirms --name can be imported afterward. Shared by check-pack-install.sh (local release gate) and `release stage` (CI publish path) so both use identical verification — catches an already-published PEER dependency that is itself broken, which static manifest checks cannot see. Surfaces the real failure reason via @npmcli/arborist directly; plain `npm install` swallows this exact failure class as an unhandled rejection with no usable error.

commands.describe: Promote already-released package versions to npm (no re-bump, no rebuild)
commands.longDescription: Publishes the CURRENT on-disk package.json versions to npm — no version bump, no rebuild. Intended to run after `release run --channel stable` (typically targeting Verdaccio via config.registry): once that run is verified, `release promote` pushes the exact same, already-committed versions to npm under the stable dist-tag.

commands.describe: Ship the tarballs `release stage` already packed to a target — no packing, no rebuild
commands.longDescription: CI-side half of the "plugin prepares, CI delivers" release flow: reads manifest.json written by `release stage` and ships those exact tarballs to --target (only "npm" is implemented this pass). Resolves {flow, channel} from --release-tag via release.flows[*].tagPattern so CI never needs to guess the flow itself — just pass the tag. commands.longDescription: Produces the actual npm tarball artifacts for a flow's already-committed package.json versions — no re-bump, no rebuild. Intended to run once in CI right after checking out a release tag; every `release deliver` target then ships these exact bytes instead of re-packing independently. commands.describe: Install a packed tarball into a throwaway consumer and confirm it imports cleanly

flags.name: repos
flags.description: Comma-separated list of repos to scope (e.g. kb-labs-cli,kb-labs-core)

flags.name: ttl
flags.description: npm registry cache TTL in hours (default: 24)

examples: devlink switch --mode=npm # Switch to npm mode (CI/CD)
devlink switch --mode=local # Switch to local mode (development)
devlink switch --mode=local --dry-run # Preview changes without applying
devlink switch --mode=npm --repos=kb-labs-cli,kb-labs-core # Switch specific repos only

manifests.describe: Run agent task (execute, plan, edit, or debug)
manifests.longDescription: Unified agent command with multiple modes: execute (default) - run task immediately, plan - generate execution plan without running, edit - modify existing files, debug - analyze errors with trace context. Supports filesystem, search, shell, memory, and user interaction tools.

flags.name: mode
flags.description: Agent mode: execute (default), plan, edit, debug

flags.name: complexity
flags.description: Task complexity (for plan mode): simple, medium, complex

flags.name: execute
flags.description: After plan is approved, immediately execute it (use with --mode=plan --approve)

flags.name: dry-run
flags.description: Preview changes without applying (for edit mode)

flags.name: debug
flags.description: Enable debug mode: emit full prompts and responses as llm:debug events

flags.name: timeout
flags.description: Abort agent execution after this many seconds (exit code 124). No timeout by default.

flags.name: budget
flags.description: Override token budget (e.g. 300000 for heavy tasks). Overrides config value.

flags.name: json
flags.description: Output structured JSON result instead of human-readable output.

display.description: Autonomous agents, tool calling, and task orchestration

commands.describe: Run agent task (execute, plan, edit, or debug)
commands.longDescription: Unified agent command with multiple modes: execute (default) - run task immediately, plan - generate execution plan without running, edit - modify existing files, debug - analyze errors with trace context. Supports filesystem, search, shell, memory, and user interaction tools.

flags.name: mode
flags.description: Agent mode: execute (default), plan, edit, debug

flags.name: complexity
flags.description: Task complexity (for plan mode): simple, medium, complex

flags.name: execute
flags.description: After plan is approved, immediately execute it (use with --mode=plan --approve)

flags.name: dry-run
flags.description: Preview changes without applying (for edit mode)

flags.name: debug
flags.description: Enable debug mode: emit full prompts and responses as llm:debug events

flags.name: timeout
flags.description: Abort agent execution after this many seconds (exit code 124). No timeout by default.

flags.name: budget
flags.description: Override token budget (e.g. 300000 for heavy tasks). Overrides config value.

flags.name: json
flags.description: Output structured JSON result instead of human-readable output.

commands.describe: Show trace statistics: tokens, cost, timing
commands.longDescription: Analyze trace file to show comprehensive statistics: iterations, LLM calls, token usage, tool usage, timing, and cost. Supports --json flag for AI agent consumption.

commands.describe: Filter trace events by type for debugging
commands.longDescription: Filter trace events by type (llm:call, tool:execution, error:captured, etc.). Use this to debug specific aspects of agent execution. Supports --json flag for programmatic access.

flags.name: type
flags.description: Event type to filter (llm:call, tool:execution, etc.)

commands.describe: View all events for a specific iteration
commands.longDescription: Show all trace events for a specific iteration number. Useful for debugging what happened in a particular loop iteration. Includes summary statistics and event timeline.

commands.describe: Inspect context window and truncations per iteration
commands.longDescription: Shows the full context timeline for debugging agent behavior. For each LLM call: what messages are in the sliding window, what was truncated/dropped, and what the LLM responded with.

commands.describe: Diagnose what went wrong in an agent run
commands.longDescription: Comprehensive diagnostic report for agent execution. Analyzes errors, context window health (drops, truncations), tool failures, LLM reasoning text, loop detection, and quality indicators. One command to understand any agent issue.

commands.describe: Show quality control report for recent agent runs
commands.longDescription: Aggregates agent KPI telemetry from analytics buffer and shows quality, token usage, tool efficiency, drift, and regression alerts. Useful for continuous quality control and cost/performance monitoring.

commands.describe: Show file change history for agent sessions
commands.longDescription: View file changes made by agents during execution. Filter by session, file, or agent. Shows timestamps, operations, and change metadata.

commands.describe: Show diff for specific file change
commands.longDescription: Display line-by-line diff for a specific file change. Shows additions, deletions, and modifications with context.

flags.name: change-id
flags.description: Change ID to show diff for

commands.describe: Rollback file changes made by agents
commands.longDescription: Rollback file changes made by agents. Supports rollback by change ID, file path, agent ID, session, or timestamp. Use --dry-run to preview changes before applying.

flags.name: file
flags.description: File path to rollback all changes for

flags.name: agent-id
flags.description: Agent ID to rollback all changes by

flags.name: session-id
flags.description: Session ID to rollback all changes in
